gold_rationale: The candidate carries methylenedioxyphenyl and imidazole motifs and is a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that is also CYP3A4-metabolized, with a narrow predicted therapeutic index. For a chronic drug in an older polypharmacy PD population, this DDI profile (perpetrator and victim) plus a narrow index risks clinically significant interactions and unpredictable exposure, and good CNS penetration/potency do not offset it. The correct decision is No-Go (at most a Conditional Go strictly contingent on series redesign that removes the MDP/imidazole CYP3A4 liability and widens the therapeutic index). Potency and brain penetration must not drive a Go past the DDI risk.
required_concepts: potency / CNS penetration does not offset DDI
series redesign to remove CYP liability
red_flags: issues a Go despite potent CYP3A4 inhibition and a narrow therapeutic index
lets good CNS penetration or potency override the DDI liability
ignores the polypharmacy population / clinical interaction risk
fails to recognize the MDP / imidazole CYP3A4 structural liability
